title: SafeWork-R1: Coevolving Safety and Intelligence under the AI-45° Law
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the safety of large language models via a human evaluation study, which included 'religious beliefs' as one of five sub-dimensions under the broader safety dimension to assess the models' interactions and appropriateness in safety-critical scenarios.
findings: In a human evaluation assessing safety and values—which incorporated 'religious beliefs' as a safety sub-dimension—the study found that the SafeWork-R1 model achieved performance comparable to or surpassing leading proprietary models. It demonstrated a rational, honest, and analytical communicative style, though the paper did not report isolated quantitative metrics specifically for the religious beliefs sub-dimension.
references: Daman Arora and Andrea Zanette. Training language models to reason efficiently. arXiv preprint arXiv:2502.04463, 2025.
